subject: Interactive transcript ownership & export safeguards for chat payloads
messages:
From: Susan Fletcher <s.fletcher@medlogic.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@medlogic.com, tom.alvarez@medlogic.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Interactive transcript ownership & export safeguards for chat payloads

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our legal & product teams about how Redwood will treat the conversational payloads we send during production:

1) Ownership/derivatives: our counsel needs a clear statement that MedLogic retains IP/ownership over inbound prompts and the verbatim chat transcripts (customer content). We also need to understand whether Redwood will ever derive models from that data (even aggregated or pseudonymized) without an explicit opt-in.

2) Export & residency lanes: for certain patient-facing workflows we need an auditable export lane (SFTP or on-prem ingestion) that ensures transcripts and any derived artefacts can be exported on demand. We also need to know the subprocessors involved in any export path.

3) Evidence: if you can provide a current subprocessor inventory and a short note on the operational safeguards (retention windows, KV cache policies, whether ephemeral tokens are stored), that will speed legal review.

Can you confirm the high-level answers and send the inventory/any annotated DPA redlines?

—Susan
Susan Fletcher
Head of Privacy, MedLogic
[sent from mobile]

From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Susan Fletcher <s.fletcher@medlogic.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interactive transcript ownership & export safeguards for chat payloads

Hi Susan —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:

- Ownership: MedLogic retains ownership of prompts and chat transcripts. Redwood does not claim ownership of customer content.
- Model improvement: By default Redwood may use telemetry to improve models; however, for enterprise customers we support an explicit opt-out ("no-adaptive-learning") that prevents customer content from being used to update or fine-tune shared models.
- Export lanes & subprocessors: We can provision an export lane (SFTP or API-based archive) and provide a current subprocessor inventory. See attached preliminary inventory and an annotated DPA with our standard operational notes.

I'll let Marissa share the ops specifics (retention, KV cache behavior, exports) and Rachel will speak to the contractual language and a proposed amendment for the no-adaptive-learning clause.

Attached: annotated_dpa_redwood_comments_v1.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_20261118.csv

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if helpful.

Jonas Weber
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Susan Fletcher <s.fletcher@medlogic.com>, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interactive transcript ownership & export safeguards for chat payloads

Hi Susan —

Operational details (summary):

- Retention: By default transient conversational state (session KV caches and step tokens) is kept for up to 24 hours and then evicted. Full transcripts persisted for customer accounts in Hosted mode are retained per the DPA default (30 days) unless the customer requests a different SLA or an export.
- KV cache & ephemeral data: KV cache entries are encrypted at rest and manually purged on request; they are not used for model training when the customer has enabled the no-adaptive-learning flag.
- Export lanes: We can provide a dedicated export lane with daily SFTP pushes (encrypted, TLS 1.3) or a webhook-based archival API. Exported files are delivered to your SFTP endpoint and retained for 14 days in our outbound transfer buffer.
- Subprocessors on export path: see inventory (rows marked "export-path"). Notable subprocessors: CloudStorageCo (US), ManagedSFTP (EU), TelemetryProxy (US).

Operational ask: if you want export to a private on-prem bucket, we can route via our Dedicated/Private offering or enable an encrypted SFTP lane with IP allowlist. That will require a short network onboarding (1–2 weeks) and a signed export SLA.

I attached an export_lanes_mapping.xlsx showing which subprocessors are involved per lane. Happy to map to any internal compliance controls you share.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
To: Susan Fletcher <s.fletcher@medlogic.com>, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interactive transcript ownership & export safeguards for chat payloads

Hi Susan —

Legal follow-up on contractual language: we've proposed a short DPA amendment clause that does three things — (1) expressly confirms that Customer retains ownership of prompts and transcripts, (2) adds an operational "no-adaptive-learning" option (customer elects at account level; if selected, Redwood will not use Customer Content for model training, evaluation, or improvement), and (3) commits to a documented export lane with named subprocessors on the record.

Two notes for negotiation:
- We can include a certification workflow for no-adaptive-learning (ops evidence pack) but we cannot guarantee absolute deletion of telemetry that has been previously replicated to internal debug stores prior to opt-out; we'll document the window and remediation steps.
- For on-prem export or Private deployment we can remove some subprocessors entirely (those moved on-prem), which improves control but adds onboarding/time.

I've attached the annotated DPA with the proposed amendment highlighted. If you accept, we'll prepare a short MSA addendum with the no-adaptive-learning flag and an implementation checklist.

—Rachel Kim
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: annotated_dpa_redwood_comments_v1.pdf]

From: Susan Fletcher <s.fletcher@medlogic.com>

Jonas / Rachel / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying questions from our side before we route to procurement: 

1) The opt-out: is the no-adaptive-learning flag reversible, and if we flip it off later will Redwood publish an audit of what data was prevented from training during the opt-out period? We need an auditable trail.

2) Export delivery: for the SFTP lane, can you confirm encryption-at-rest on the outbound buffer and whether file names are salted/obfuscated? Our security team requires non-guessable file identifiers and that files be encrypted at rest while in transit staging.

3) Subprocessor deletions: when you say subprocessors can be removed under a Private deployment, can you be specific about which ones (CloudStorageCo, TelemetryProxy) would no longer be in scope? Any checklist or matrix helps procurement.

If you can send short, bullet answers we can attach to the procurement packet.

Best,
Susan

From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Susan Fletcher <s.fletcher@medlogic.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interactive transcript ownership & export safeguards for chat payloads

Susan —

Short bullets to attach to procurement: 

1) Opt-out reversibility & audit: The no-adaptive-learning flag is reversible. When enabled, we tag incoming records and exclude them from any training pipelines; our audit system logs flag changes and the record counts excluded per day. We will provide an ops evidence pack documenting counts and a signed attestation for the opt-out window.

2) Export delivery: Outbound buffer files are encrypted at rest using AES-256. File names are salted with a 128-bit random prefix and are not guessable. Files in the outbound buffer persist for a configurable window (default 14 days) and are removed after successful delivery.

3) Subprocessor scope under Private deployment: If MedLogic opts for a Private deployment or a Dedicated on-prem export lane, the following subprocessors are removable from scope: CloudStorageCo (object store), TelemetryProxy (event routing). ManagedSFTP would remain only if you elect Redwood-managed SFTP; otherwise you control the SFTP endpoint and ManagedSFTP is not used. We'll include a matrix in the MSA addendum.

Next steps: Rachel will drop the redline for the short addendum and Marissa will attach the export_lanes_mapping.xlsx showing which subprocessors are on each path. If this looks acceptable to procurement, we'll schedule a 30-min technical onboarding to scope the export lane.

Thanks —
Jonas

[Attachments referenced: annotated_dpa_redwood_comments_v1.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_20261118.csv; export_lanes_mapping.xlsx]
